questions.q: What two pillars does the author's diet rest on?
a: Eating fewer calories and getting the right amount of protein
Eating more often and cutting all fats from meals
Counting carbs precisely and avoiding vegetables
Fasting every other day and training intensely
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes an adequate-protein, low-carb, high-fat approach built on those two habits.

questions.q: Why does the summary warn against eating too much protein?
a: It activates mTOR, which blocks the body from clearing cellular debris
It raises leptin and makes the body store extra water
It shuts down mitochondria and stops energy production
It prevents the body from absorbing any dietary fat
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that excess protein or carbs switch on mTOR and hinder cleanup.

questions.q: Roughly how much protein does the book recommend per kilogram of lean body mass?
a: About 0.5 grams
About 2 grams
About 4 grams
About 0.05 grams
questions.why: Lesson 2 gives 0.5 grams per kilo of lean mass and walks through a sample calculation.

questions.q: What eating window does peak fasting recommend?
a: Eating for 6 to 11 hours and fasting for 13 to 18
Eating for 12 hours and fasting for 12
Eating for 3 hours and fasting for 21
Eating whenever hungry and fasting only at night
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes a daily window of roughly six to eleven hours of eating.

questions.q: What does the author advise about eating before sleep?
a: Stop eating three to six hours before bedtime
Have a small high-carb snack to sleep better
Eat a protein-rich meal right before bed
Only avoid food if you wake up during the night
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to finish eating several hours before going to bed.
